messages:
jess: heads-up — we started seeing a sudden spike of 502/504s from Hosted API around 10:03 UTC. Customers A, B reporting timeouts and downstream errors. seeing lots of upstream resets in edge logs. anyone oncall?

mike: oncall here. initial grep of envoy access logs shows a big increase in 502 from edge-proxy clusters  us-east-1-edge-1 / us-east-1-edge-2. sample lines: 
```
[10:03:12] "POST /v1/complete" 502 - upstream_reset upstream_reset_before_response_tx
[10:03:13] "POST /v1/chat" 504 - response_timeout
```
trace ids: trace=tr-0a1b2c3d, tr-0a1b2c3e

sara: also seeing gRPC auth cache latencies jump to 400-1200ms around same time in auth-cache-prod.  p99 auth latency went from 45ms -> 900ms. that service pops in front of model routers for token validation.

anthony: could be h2 connection pool exhaustion. when upstream auth is slow, edge keeps connections open waiting and h2 max concurrent streams gets exhausted -> envoys return 502s or upstream reset. check h2 metrics: active_streams, queued_streams, conn_reuse.

jess: good call. mike, can you pull h2_conn_pool_* metrics from prometheus for the affected clusters between 09:50-10:20? also include envoy cluster_manager stats.

mike: grabbing now. quick paste: 
```
edge_auth_cluster.active_connections: spikes from 30->120
edge_auth_cluster.pending_requests: 0->350
edge_auth_cluster.max_streams_per_connection: 100
edge_auth_cluster.upstream_rq_pending_overflow: 0->172
```
looks like pending requests queueing.

infra-bot: [ALERT] cluster "edge-auth" pending_overflow > 100 (value=172) at 2026-03-12T10:04:05Z

kerry: copying from logs: envoy reported "upstream connection termination" and "stream reset: CANCEL" repeatedly. also a notable pattern where many client streams stayed open for ~30s before reset.

sara: reproduction steps from support: 1) hit /v1/complete with long auth token validation (simulate with sleep on auth service) 2) send many concurrent requests 3) observe upstream pending queue grow -> 502s. i spun a test: `hey -c 400 -n 400 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://api.redwood.example/v1/complete` and saw 40% 502 in 10s.

anthony: that matches h2 pool drain scenario. root cause hypothesis: auth-cache-backed token validation degraded (GC spike / cache eviction) causing auth service to respond slowly -> edge's upstream connections saturate and Envoy returns immediate 502/504.

mike: mitigation options (short-term): 
- scale auth-cache replicas by +50% (pod horizontal scale)
- restart a few thrift backends that are in high-latency state
- temporarily increase max-connections or max-requests-per-connection on edge->auth cluster (careful)
- enable route-level retries for auth failures with small per-route timeout

jess: do step 1 now: Sara, can you scale auth-cache? Anthony, add a rapid circuit-breaker rule so we fail-fast to auth and let caller fall back to unauth path where allowed?

sara: scaling auth-cache to 6 -> 9 replicas now (HPA bump). patch applied. watching metrics.

deploy-bot: rollout started: deployment/auth-cache v2.3.1 -> v2.3.1 (scale: 6->9). status: 3 pods created, 6 ready -> 9 ready expected.

mike: slight improvement visible: pending_overflow down to 60, p99 auth latency down to ~120ms. client 502 rate dropped from 43% -> 9% over 3 minutes.

anthony: follow-up config change: i've queued a conservative envoy change to reduce idle stream timeout from 60s -> 20s for edge->auth route and set max_requests_per_connection: 200 -> 400 to improve reuse. will deploy to canary edge cluster only first.

jess: please hold on wide rollout until we confirm no regression. also we need a temporary customer message: set expectations for a degraded window ~10:00-10:30 UTC. @support lead draft?

kerry: drafted notify to affected customers and CSMs. TL;DR: intermittent 502/504 due to auth validation latency causing upstream saturation; mitigation underway (scaled auth-cache). ETA full recovery 10:45 UTC. sending now.

infra-bot: [NOTICE] canary envoy patch applied to us-east-1-edge-canary: idle_timeout=20s, max_requests_per_connection=400 at 2026-03-12T10:12:04Z

mike: after canary patch throughput improved, further drop in 502s to under 2% for canary. rolling patch to remaining edges in 2 waves.

sara: auth-cache GC fix PR merged (reduces cache miss penalty). will schedule a rolling restart on stable nodes after traffic eases.

jess: summary / next steps:
- root cause: auth-cache latency spike -> h2 connection pool exhaustion at edge -> 502/504s
- immediate mitigations: scale auth-cache, envoy idle timeout reduction on edge->auth, circuit breaker config (canary then roll).
- medium: deploy GC fix and proactive HPA tuning for auth-cache, add alerting on auth pending_overflow > 50
- long: consider moving auth validation to async token verification path to avoid blocking request stream, and add request-level hedging for short auth timeouts.

anthony: i'll open infra ticket: INF-2026-321 for config changes and runbook updates.

jess: thanks everyone. last check: last_message_ts set to 2087654988 when we confirmed low error rate and customer notice sent. leaving this thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
